createpackage.ponder.kinetic_batch_linki: FTB Ultimine: Batch Link and Unlink
This optional chapter requires FTB Ultimine. Hold the Machine Linker throughout; installing the mod does not link machines automatically.
First release the Ultimine key and sneak key. Right-click the provider with the linker to select the host. Its target must already face a valid Deployer.

Your Ultimine activation key is [%s]. Normally hold it with Sneak and scroll to choose a shape. If Ultimine itself is bound to Shift, its shape menu uses Ctrl instead. Check the preview and your Controls settings.

Choose a shape whose preview covers the desired machines. Only loaded blocks matching the clicked block ID and the provider target type are accepted. Selection size is limited by FTB settings; use several clicks if necessary.
Keep [%s] held, RELEASE Sneak, then right-click a selected machine with the linker: this adds the matching selection in one operation. Do not click the provider for this step.

Install a Parallel Card through the upgrade slot or sneak-right-click. Links may be saved without a card, but no card uses only the front target. One card allows 16 total machines; the front target counts once.
For batch removal, keep [%s] and Sneak held, then right-click a machine in the selection. This removes links, not blocks, and does not remove the provider front target.

Release the Ultimine key before sneak-right-clicking the provider: that clears all saved extra links and the linker selection. For Mechanical Crafters, link one representative per independent group, not every block in a wall.
This is a machine set, not an ordered assembly route. G is not used here. If no preview or batch action appears, check mod installation, the configured key, conflicts, hunger and the selected shape.
createpackage.ponder.kinetic_crushing_wh: Facing a wheel block is rejected. This adapter targets create:crushing_wheel_controller, the invisible processing block between two wheels; clicking a wheel does not redirect to it.
Place matching-axis wheels with one block between them and drive them in opposite directions. In this vertical example they pull downward, producing a valid controller in the middle gap.
Place the provider beside the middle gap. A temporary support block on the near side makes placement easy; attach the provider to its far face, then remove the support.
From ALL, right-click the provider NORTH face with a wrench. It now targets SOUTH into the middle controller. Connect powered ME on another face.

The input goes into the controller, not into either wheel. For a downward controller, place a recoverable Depot or Belt directly below the GAP; the provider collects there. A loose floor or arbitrary chest is not equivalent.
The colored gap outline is a teaching marker. The real controller is invisible and has no normal black selection outline; F3 Targeted Block can confirm its ID and coordinates.
Select the provider with the linker. For another crushing pair, link its middle controller, not either wheel and not the output Depot. Each pair needs its own correct output and drive.

To aim at the invisible target, place a temporary visible block BEHIND the second gap. Stand in front with your eye level through the gap, and aim at that reference block; the controller is hit first.
Use F3 to confirm create:crushing_wheel_controller, then right-click with the linker. No black outline is expected. Remove the reference afterward; sneak-right-click the same target to unlink it.
Parallel Cards enable extra linked controllers. The front controller is already a target. Repeat for independent pairs; linking the two wheel blocks does not create two processing machines.
createpackage.ponder.kinetic_machine_wor: Mechanical Saw: Orientation and Exit Side
Target the Saw block itself, with its blade facing UP, and give its shaft real rotation. A sideways or stopped Saw is rejected even if its item inventory can be reached.
The input enters the Saw. In this direction it ejects EAST into the adjacent Depot at the SAME height. The provider sets the Saw filter from the pattern main output and recovers from this exit.

Reversing rotation reverses the exit. The old output Depot is no longer the output; put a recoverable carrier at the new exit. Motor panel signs depend on orientation, so check the actual movement direction.

The reversed example now has a west Depot and the provider moved to a free side. A valid output must accept the Saw ejection and expose an item handler; an arbitrary chest or bare ground is not enough.
Mixer and Press: Target the Machine, Supply the Basin
Face the MIXER, not the Basin. The Basin must be two blocks below the mixer. Pattern items and fluids go there and products are collected there; a Depot cannot replace the mixer Basin.
Drive the mixer through its cogwheel and satisfy the recipe speed and heat requirements. The burner shown supplies heat beneath the Basin; a powered ME connection does not provide rotation or heat.
The Press also works two blocks below itself. With a Basin, it receives basin recipe inputs. For ordinary single-item pressing, place a Depot or Belt at that work position instead.
Bind the actual processing machines when adding parallel targets. Each needs its own valid work position; do not link their Basins or Depots as if those were extra mixers or presses.
Spout: Separate Item and Fluid Destinations
Target the SPOUT itself. Place a Depot or Belt two blocks below it. The pattern item goes onto that working position, while the pattern fluid is inserted directly into the Spout tank.
A Spout needs the required fluid but no rotational shaft. After filling, the provider recovers the product from the same Depot or Belt. Extra linked Spouts each need their own free working position.
createpackage.ponder.kinetic_mechanical_: Mechanical Crafters: Recognition and Automatic Layout
Build a four-neighbor connected wall of Mechanical Crafters, all facing the same direction and in one plane. This real crushing-wheel recipe uses a 5x5 shape without its four corners: 21 crafters.
Power the integrated cogwheels through an adjacent cogwheel. A shaft or motor directly behind a crafter is not a shaft connection. Neighboring gears rotate in opposite directions, as shown.

The provider must touch a crafter and have its target face point at that block. ALL has no target. It can recognize the connected wall from that one entrance; no G scan or linker selection is required for the front group.

Encode an AE2 PROCESSING pattern, not a normal crafting pattern: 16 Andesite Alloy + 4 matching Planks + 1 matching Stone -> 2 Crushing Wheels. The adapter obtains the large layout from the real recipe; do not force it into a 3x3 pattern.
After a valid job passes planning, the provider arranges the required arrows and shared input groups and supplies each recipe cell. You do not need to hand-turn every arrow or merge inputs first.
Here the provider touches the edge IN the wall plane, so it can also receive the final product directly. This is different from a provider touching only the wall front or back.

Keep ingredient cells uncovered and empty. Matching normal crafting-table recipes depend on Create server settings. If the wall is too small, disconnected, unpowered or occupied, check the specific Goggles/Jade rejection reason.
Mechanical Crafters: Outputs and Independent Groups
A provider behind the wall can target the crafter in front of it, but crafter arrows move only within the wall plane. Target recognition and a usable product exit are separate requirements.
Put a chest or Depot directly next to an edge crafter IN the wall plane. It need not touch the provider. The provider plans toward that outlet and collects its products remotely.
Without this accessible inventory, planning reports no usable output container. Dropping a chest nearby, above the wall or behind it does not create a valid in-plane exit.

For parallel work, separate complete crafter groups with air and give each its own outlet. Add a Parallel Card, select the provider with the linker, then link ONE representative crafter in each extra group. The front group is already present.

Do not batch-link every block in one wall as though each were an independent machine. Stored links are coordinate-based; repeated members of the same working chain do not create extra production lines.
createpackage.ponder.kinetic_pattern_pro: Place the provider beside the machine itself. The default ALL setting has no machine target.
Starting from ALL, right-click the WEST face with a wrench to target the machine to the EAST.
Connect ME on a non-target face. This marks the connection only: the real network needs power, a channel, storage, a crafting CPU, and a submitted job.
The motor and shaft power the Deployer separately. The provider supplies ingredients; it does not provide rotation.
Preload Sand Paper. Put a processing pattern for Rose Quartz -> Polished Rose Quartz in the provider; the tool can stay in the hand.
When AE dispatches the pattern, its first item input goes to the working position, two blocks along the Deployer's facing.
The finished item is collected from that same working position and returned to ME storage. Keep space available in the network.
A Millstone keeps its own output
Face the Millstone itself and power its bottom shaft. A processing pattern supplies its internal input inventory.
For example, mill Granite into Red Sand. The Millstone's own inventory holds both the input and the resulting output.
Recover the output directly from the Millstone and return it to ME. No separate output Depot is required.
Saws and crushing controllers differ: provide a recoverable belt or Depot at their computed output. A Saw must face up; its speed sign sets the exit side.
More patterns, the same machine logic
The regular Kinetic Pattern Provider stores 9 patterns. Right-click to open its pattern and upgrade slots.
The Extended version shows 36 patterns per page. It defaults to 1 page; server configuration can unlock up to 9 pages, or 324 slots.
Reducing the page setting keeps pages containing saved patterns accessible. Extra pattern storage does not increase machine concurrency.
Both versions accept up to 4 Parallel Cards: no card runs 1 machine; each card allows 16 total matching machines, up to 64, including the front machine.
createpackage.ponder.mechanical_route_to: Machine Linker: One Ordered Route
Build the transport first: a powered belt moves east under four downward deployers, each two blocks above it. The end stop keeps items available for collection.
This real recipe uses one gold sheet and the Silicon, Logic, Engineering and Calculation Presses in that order. All four tools are kept; three passes produce one normal Package Distributor.
1. Right-click the Basic Distributor with the Machine Linker to select the host. The normal Distributor uses the same linking procedure.
2. Right-click the first belt segment to mark the input. The distributor supplies the base item here; its own facing does not choose the input.
3. Right-click all four deployers in process order, from left to right. Link the machines themselves, not every belt segment beneath them.
4. Mark the final belt segment last. It is the output: unfinished items return to the input, and finished products return to ME storage.

Put the linker away and right-click to open the Basic Distributor GUI. Insert an encoded processing pattern: 1 gold sheet → 1 normal Package Distributor. Connect powered ME storage and a crafting CPU to request it.
Converter: Put the Route on a Pattern
The Advanced Distributor reads routes from Mechanical Package Patterns. With the converter, begin by marking the input; there is no distributor host to select.
Mark the four deployers in order, then the final belt segment. The converter now holds input → four deployers → output for this physical line.
Right-click AIR with the converter to open its GUI. Put the encoded AE2 processing pattern, 1 gold sheet → 1 normal Package Distributor, in an input slot and press Convert.
Take the Mechanical Package Pattern from the output slot. It contains the original encoded pattern, this ordered route and its encoder information; it is not a physical parcel of ingredients.
Put the held tool away. Empty-hand right-click the Advanced Distributor to open its GUI, then place the Mechanical Package Pattern in a pattern slot. It needs a powered ME network and a crafting CPU.
An existing encoded Mechanical Package Pattern is also a route tool. While holding it, you can append, replace or remove its own marks without changing the encoded recipe.
Append, Edit and Auto-route
Append is the default mode: right-click a machine to add its mark at the end; sneak-right-click a marked machine to remove that clicked mark.
Left-click AIR to switch between Append and Edit. These ordered modes work for converters, encoded Mechanical Package Patterns and linkers bound to normal or Basic Distributors.
In Edit mode, scroll to select a route mark first. Right-click a valid route block to replace that selected position while preserving its place in the order.
In Edit mode, sneak-right-click a valid route block to remove the SELECTED mark. This differs from Append mode, which removes the mark you clicked.
To clear a stored distributor route, sneak-right-click its host with the linker in Append mode. To clear the converter's own route, sneak-right-click AIR with the converter.
For auto-route, start with a clear route in Append mode: mark the input first and output second, then press G while holding the tool. A linker must already be bound to a normal or Basic Distributor.

G rebuilds the route between its first and last marks. Endpoints must be different depots or belt blocks on the same Y level. It scans a straight corridor and adds deployers aimed at its stations and spouts two blocks above them.

A single L-shaped bend is supported only when enabled in server config, with a depot or belt at the corner. Default maximum length is 512 blocks. G does not build transport, connect power or discover presses and saws.
Kinetic Pattern Provider links are a set of parallel machines, not an ordered assembly route. They do not support these Edit-mode controls or G auto-route.
createpackage.ponder.package_distributor: Choose a Distributor and Connect ME
The normal Distributor needs an adjacent AE2 Pattern Provider. Open that provider GUI and put the processing patterns there. Link the assembly route to the distributor itself.
The Basic Distributor contains its own provider with 9 pattern slots. Open its GUI empty-handed. It stores one ordered route and runs one job at a time.
The Advanced Distributor has 36 pattern slots. Each Mechanical Package Pattern stores its own route, so one distributor can serve several independent assembly lines.
Controllers here mark ME connections only. A working build needs AE power, available channels, storage containing the materials and a crafting CPU. This is not a complete ME network simulation.

Distributors supply ingredients and recover outputs for a real Create line. They do not make physical parcels, move items between stations or provide rotation. Kinetic Pattern Providers serve individual machines instead.
A Complete Three-pass Assembly Cycle
Build the full transport: six belt segments move east under four downward deployers, two blocks above the belt. Both the belt and deployers have power. The end stop prevents dropped outputs.

Select the Basic Distributor, then link the first belt segment, the Silicon, Logic, Engineering and Calculation deployers, and the final belt segment, in that order. The first and last carriers define input and output.
Open the GUI empty-handed and insert a processing pattern: 1 gold sheet -> 1 normal Package Distributor. The actual recipe takes three passes through four steps: 12 operations.
Each deployer holds one matching AE2 Press. All four tools are kept. Preload them as shown, or let the distributor take missing tools from ME. Do not encode three copies of every tool.
Pass 1/3: the same workpiece visits all four powered deployers.
Pass 1 finished: extract the unfinished item and return the SAME stack, with its progress, to the input.
Pass 2/3: the same workpiece visits all four powered deployers.
Pass 2 finished: extract the unfinished item and return the SAME stack, with its progress, to the input.
Pass 3/3: the same workpiece visits all four powered deployers.
After operation 12, the finished Distributor reaches the output and returns directly to ME storage. All four tools remain in the deployers.
Advanced: Independent Routes in Parallel
Build two complete independent copies. Each has its own input, four deployers and output. They may share ME and a power source, but must not share processing inventories.
Convert two copies of the same processing pattern. Each Mechanical Package Pattern stores one complete ordered route: one for the front line and one for the back line.
Open the Advanced Distributor GUI empty-handed and insert both Mechanical Package Patterns. There are 36 pattern slots. Plain AE2 patterns cannot be used here.

Install a Parallel Card by sneak-right-clicking, or use the upgrade slot. No cards: one job. Default limits are 16 jobs with one card and 64 with four, subject to independent routes and available AE work.
Equivalent encoded patterns are dispatched to idle equivalent routes in rotation. These two jobs can be at different steps while both machines work.
Routes sharing any marked block cannot run together on this distributor. Cards increase capacity; they do not make a shared input, output or deployer safe for simultaneous jobs.
No external provider is needed. Keep the physical lines independent throughout: the overlap check cannot identify shared resources omitted from the marks.
Pattern Inputs, Power and Retry Rules

Recipe selection starts with the primary output, then uses the base ingredient and step inputs to disambiguate. Missing candidates, tied best matches or unused inputs reject the pattern before normal execution.
Encode one base item per full assembly. Multiply consumed deployer items and filling amounts by the loop count. Kept tools only need one copy, preloaded or supplied from ME.

Deployer ingredients go directly into their deployers; fluids go into their linked spouts. Remaining supplies wait when a target is full. Ingredients do not enter a particular face of the distributor model.
AE power and channels run the distributor. Actual rotational power runs belts, deployers, presses and saws; spouts need no rotation. Route marks replace neither transport nor missing machines.

This gold-sheet example is deterministic. For other probabilistic recipes, byproducts return to ME and another full material round is supplied if the requested main product is still missing. Never list optional byproducts as required outputs.

Reserve refill materials and ME storage space. Crafting missing refill materials automatically is off by default. Goggles or Jade report missing supplies, blocked targets, inactive ME or rejected patterns.
createpackage.ponder.parallel_card_kinet: A full one-card setup: 16 Deployers, each with its own Depot and Sand Paper. Connected shafts through each row are powered by the motor at its end.
Before installing a card, only the machine directly east of the provider can receive work: 1/1 active machine. The other 15 stay empty.
Select the provider with the Machine Linker, then right-click all 15 extra Deployers. The front machine is already counted; it is not a seventeenth target.
Install card 1/1 by sneak-right-clicking, or use an upgrade slot. The current limit is 16 total machines.
Full load: 16/16. ME supplies 16 separate jobs and enough Rose Quartz. Every machine receives an input at the same moment and processes it with its own held tool.

All 16 products are collected from the 16 individual working positions and returned to ME. The provider connection shown still needs powered storage, a channel and a crafting CPU with enough parallel work.
Cards increase available machine slots, not output per recipe or rotational power. One card caps at 16, four at 64, including the front machine. Fewer valid links means fewer active machines.
Four-card maximum: a real 8 by 8 array of 64 Deployers. Each row has its own connected motor; each machine has a separate Depot and Sand Paper.
Use the previous linking procedure for all 63 extra machines. The front machine plus these links makes exactly 64 targets. Keep every target loaded and use the same machine block type.
Install card 1/4 by sneak-right-clicking, or use an upgrade slot. The current limit is 16 total machines.
Install card 2/4 by sneak-right-clicking, or use an upgrade slot. The current limit is 32 total machines.
Install card 3/4 by sneak-right-clicking, or use an upgrade slot. The current limit is 48 total machines.
Install card 4/4 by sneak-right-clicking, or use an upgrade slot. The current limit is 64 total machines.
Full load: 64/64. ME supplies 64 separate jobs and enough Rose Quartz. Every machine receives an input at the same moment and processes it with its own held tool.

All 64 products are collected from the 64 individual working positions and returned to ME. The provider connection shown still needs powered storage, a channel and a crafting CPU with enough parallel work.
Cards increase available machine slots, not output per recipe or rotational power. One card caps at 16, four at 64, including the front machine. Fewer valid links means fewer active machines.
createpackage.ponder.parallel_card_advan: Parallel Cards also fit Advanced Package Distributors. With no card, the distributor accepts 1 active assembly job across its routed patterns.
By default, 1 card allows 16 active jobs and 4 allow 64. The server can set 1-64 jobs per card; this setting does not change Kinetic Providers' fixed 16 machines per card.
Actual parallel work needs independent, powered assembly lines and a routed pattern for each. Any shared route position blocks concurrent use, including a shared input or output.
Two usable independent routes can run at most two jobs, even with a 16-job card. A card does not clone a route, build transport, or supply machine power.
